references.text: The context for Jesus' words: the Passover lamb had to be slaughtered, and Peter and John were sent to prepare the Passover meal ([ref:Luk 22:7-8|Luke 22:7-8]). Jesus' strong desire to eat this meal is connected to the preparations that had been made.

The Passover meal originated in God's command to Israel in Egypt. Jesus longed to celebrate precisely this meal – the Passover (τὸ πάσχα) – which pointed forward to his own sacrifice as the Lamb of God ([ref:2 Mos 12:3-11|Exodus 12:3-11]).
The Passover celebration was given as an eternal ordinance for Israel. Jesus fulfills the deeper meaning of this celebration through his suffering and death ([ref:2 Mos 12:14|Exodus 12:14]).

Jesus continues by saying that he will not eat the Passover meal again until it has been fulfilled in God's kingdom ([ref:Luk 22:16|Luke 22:16]). This shows that his longing in verse 15 is connected to the eschatological significance of the meal.

Jesus' desire to eat this Passover meal with the disciples aimed at instituting the new covenant through his body and blood – the Lord's Supper as a replacement for the old Passover meal ([ref:Luk 22:19-20|Luke 22:19-20]).

Jesus had already turned his face toward Jerusalem with firm determination, fully aware that he was going to his suffering (πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν). His longing for this final meal is part of the same purposefulness ([ref:Luk 9:51|Luke 9:51]).
Matthew's parallel account of the preparation and celebration of the last Passover meal with the disciples ([ref:Matt 26:17-19|Matthew 26:17-19]).
Mark's parallel account of the last Passover meal, where Jesus makes preparations to eat the Passover with his disciples ([ref:Mark 14:12-16|Mark 14:12-16]).
John emphasizes that Jesus knew his hour had come and that he loved his own to the end. This reflects the same love and longing that Jesus expresses in Luke 22:15 ([ref:Joh 13:1|John 13:1]).
The prophecy of the suffering servant who was led like a lamb to slaughter connects Jesus' impending suffering (παθεῖν) to the symbolism of the Passover lamb ([ref:Jes 53:7|Isaiah 53:7]).

Paul identifies Christ as our Passover lamb who has been sacrificed. Jesus' longing to eat the Passover meal points to the fact that he himself is the true Passover lamb ([ref:1 Kor 5:7|1 Corinthians 5:7]).

Jesus looked forward to the joy that awaited him on the other side of suffering. His longing for this final meal was part of the purposeful movement toward the cross and resurrection ([ref:Hebr 12:2|Hebrews 12:2]).
